text: In MVC architecture, which component is responsible for presenting data to the user?
answerA: Model
answerB: View
answerC: Controller
answerD: Repository

text: What is a possible disadvantage of MVC in a small, simple system?
answerA: It does not allow multiple views of the same data.
answerB: It requires a remote database.
answerC: It prevents data from being changed.
answerD: It may introduce unnecessary code and complexity.

text: What is an advantage of Layered Architecture?
answerA: An entire layer can be replaced if its interface remains unchanged.
answerB: Every layer must use exactly the same code.
answerC: Layers never need to communicate.
answerD: All operations run in the presentation layer.

text: Why can Layered Architecture reduce performance?
answerA: It prohibits unit testing.
answerB: It requires a separate server for every layer.
answerC: A request may need to pass through and be processed by several layers.
answerD: Its components cannot be replaced.

text: What is an advantage of Client–Server Architecture?
answerA: Each client must implement all services on its own.
answerB: It prevents clients from sharing services.
answerC: It always removes dependence on the network.
answerD: A server can provide the same shared service to many clients.

text: What is a possible disadvantage of Client–Server Architecture?
answerA: It cannot use a shared data store.
answerB: A server failure may make the service it provides unavailable.
answerC: The client and server must run on the same computer.
answerD: Servers cannot be distributed across a network.

text: What is the central principle of Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters)?
answerA: Keeping core business logic independent of user interfaces and external systems.
answerB: Putting all business logic inside the View component.
answerC: Requiring every component to use the same database.
answerD: Replacing all application classes with one server.

text: What does CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) separate?
answerA: Java code from code written in other languages.
answerB: Desktop user interfaces from mobile user interfaces.
answerC: Commands that change data from queries that read data.
answerD: User permissions from configuration files.

text: What is a possible challenge of Event-Driven Architecture?
answerA: New types of events cannot be introduced.
answerB: All functionality must be stored in one class.
answerC: New event consumers cannot be added.
answerD: Tracing execution and debugging asynchronous event flows can be difficult.

text: According to The Architecture of Open Source Applications, what does Eclipse's plug-in architecture enable?
answerA: Running an IDE without any software components.
answerB: Extending the core platform with independently developed plug-ins.
answerC: Requiring all development tools to be written in one file.
answerD: Preventing external developers from extending the platform.

text: What is a major advantage of Microservices Architecture?
answerA: Different services can be deployed independently.
answerB: All services must be updated at the same time.
answerC: Services never need network communication.
answerD: All services must use one shared database.

text: What is a possible disadvantage of Microservices Architecture?
answerA: The system cannot be divided into separate services.
answerB: All services must run on one computer.
answerC: Coordinating operations and maintaining data consistency across distributed services can be complex.
answerD: Individual services cannot be deployed independently.

text: When may Monolithic Architecture be a suitable choice?
answerA: When every component must be deployed separately.
answerB: When developing a small system where straightforward initial development and deployment are important.
answerC: When components must never communicate with each other.
answerD: When each operation requires a separate server.

text: What is a possible disadvantage of using CQRS?
answerA: Reading and writing operations cannot be separated.
answerB: Every read query must modify data.
answerC: Read performance cannot be optimized independently.
answerD: Keeping read and write models consistent may add complexity.

text: What is an advantage of Event-Driven Architecture when multiple consumers handle events?
answerA: A new event consumer can be added without changing the event publisher.
answerB: Every consumer must directly call every other consumer.
answerC: Asynchronous event processing is impossible.
answerD: Every event must be triggered manually by a user.

text: Who is responsible for prioritizing the Product Backlog?
answerA: Scrum Master
answerB: Product Owner
answerC: Every end user independently
answerD: Database administrator

text: Which approach best reflects Agile development?
answerA: Deliver the entire product only at the end
answerB: Avoid customer feedback until release
answerC: Develop in short cycles and adapt using feedback
answerD: Freeze all requirements permanently

text: During a sprint review, stakeholders suggest a change to a completed feature. Where should the proposed improvement be considered for future work?
answerA: In the Product Backlog
answerB: Only in the executable JAR
answerC: In the code without team discussion
answerD: In the previous sprint completed-task records

text: A team demonstrates a working increment, then discusses why integration caused delays and how to improve its collaboration. Which two Scrum events serve these purposes, respectively?
answerA: Daily Scrum and Sprint Planning
answerB: Sprint Retrospective and Sprint Review
answerC: Backlog Refinement and Daily Scrum
answerD: Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective

text: What is the main purpose of regression testing?
answerA: Check that previously working functionality still works after changes
answerB: Replace all manual tests
answerC: Measure the number of developers
answerD: Verify only newly added features

text: Which activity examines source code for defects without executing it?
answerA: Acceptance testing
answerB: Load testing
answerC: Program inspection
answerD: System testing

text: After adding a second die to a game, a previously working player setup test fails. Which type of testing is most directly intended to reveal this problem?
answerA: Usability testing
answerB: Regression testing
answerC: Installation testing
answerD: New-feature testing only

text: A team checks whether its design satisfies the approved requirements from the preceding phase and later checks whether the finished product satisfies the original requirements. What are these activities, respectively?
answerA: Validation and verification
answerB: Inspection and regression testing
answerC: Qualification and inspection
answerD: Verification and validation

text: What is the main purpose of the Factory Method pattern?
answerA: Hide all application data
answerB: Notify subscribers automatically
answerC: Control object creation without requiring the client to know the concrete class
answerD: Force each class to have only one instance

text: In the Observer pattern, what does a subject do when a relevant state change occurs?
answerA: Notifies its registered observers
answerB: Creates a new copy of every observer
answerC: Deletes all observers automatically
answerD: Waits for each observer to poll it

text: Which pattern defines the outline of an algorithm while allowing subclasses to customize selected steps?
answerA: Observer
answerB: Template Method
answerC: Singleton
answerD: Factory Method

text: A question engine keeps references to dialog listeners after each game ends. Old dialogs continue receiving events and cannot be garbage-collected. Which change best addresses the Observer-specific problem?
answerA: Make the question engine a singleton
answerB: Create a new event for every listener
answerC: Remove observer registrations when their game or dialog ends
answerD: Replace all event data with strings

text: Several importers must always validate a file, parse its records and save the result in that order. Only parsing differs by format. Which design best enforces this sequence while supporting new formats?
answerA: Let each importer implement the entire workflow independently
answerB: Place all parsing inside the UI
answerC: Use an Observer to trigger the steps in an unspecified order
answerD: Define a final template method with an overridable parsing step

text: A requirement states that a game must accept two to four players. Another requires the interface to respond within 200 milliseconds. How should these requirements be classified?
answerA: Functional and non-functional, respectively
answerB: Both non-functional
answerC: Both functional
answerD: Non-functional and functional, respectively
source: Lecture02-Software Components in the Project Life Cycle.pdf — PDF page 11–15

text: One requirement permits two to four players, while another rejects every setup containing four players. Both are individually clear. Which requirements-quality property is primarily violated?
answerA: Completeness
answerB: Consistency
answerC: Traceability
answerD: Performance
source: Lecture02-Software Components in the Project Life Cycle.pdf — PDF page 14
